entry.title: Introducing Automatic Security Audits for AI
entry.summary:
AI coding assistants move fast. They can refactor modules, add dependencies, and wire up integrations before you've finished reading the diff. That speed is valuable, but security issues can slip in just as quickly: hardcoded API keys, string-concatenated SQL queries, debug endpoints that never get removed. So we built something to help catch these issues early.
mrq now scans your code changes for common security vulnerabilities automatically. Every snapshot triggers a background analysis looking for: Hardcoded secrets, API keys, and credentials SQL injection patterns XSS vulnerabilities
Exposed sensitive data Insecure configurations Debug code that shouldn't ship Results appear in your dashboard. If something gets flagged, you'll see a warning on that snapshot with details about what was found and where.
Issues are displayed inline with your snapshot history. Traditional security scanning happens in CI/CD, often hours after code was written. By then, the context is gone. With mrq, feedback is immediate. You're still in the middle of your session when an issue gets flagged. You can fix it while everything is fresh. This is experimental. Security analysis is hard, and we're using AI to identify patterns. There will be false positives and false negatives. This is not a replacement for proper security audits, code review, or dedicated scanning tools in your pipeline. Think of it as an early warning system. A nudge to double-check something before it gets committed. Security audits are available on paid plans (Starter, Pro, Team). The feature runs automatically with no configuration needed. Try it out →

entry.title: SaaS Trends That Are Reshaping Cloud Software and Modern Development
entry.summary: The SaaS industry is evolving faster than ever, and it’s no longer just about delivering software through the cloud. Today, SaaS trends are redefining how developers build products, how businesses scale, and how users interact with technology. One of the biggest shifts we’re seeing is the deep integration of AI into SaaS platforms. AI is no longer a “future feature.” It’s now part of everyday tools—helping with automation, analytics, personalization, and smarter decision-making. For developers, this means building systems that are more data-aware and intelligent from day one. Another major trend is the move toward highly scalable, cloud-native architectures. Modern SaaS products are being designed to grow globally without performance issues. Microservices, containerization, and serverless computing are becoming standard choices, allowing teams to deploy faster and adapt quickly to changing user needs. Security and privacy are also taking center stage. As SaaS products handle more sensitive data, users expect stronger protection by default. This is pushing developers to adopt security-first approaches, including better authentication, encryption, and compliance awareness during development—not as an afterthought. We’re also seeing SaaS platforms become more flexible and customer-centric. Businesses want tools that integrate easily with their existing stack and adapt to their workflows. For developers, this means focusing more on APIs, integrations, and modular design. I’ve shared a simple and practical breakdown of current SaaS trends and how they impact digital businesses and development teams in my blog. You can read it here: https://kazimdigiworld.blogspot.com I’d love to hear from other developers: Which SaaS trends are you actively using? How is AI changing the products you’re building? What challenges do you see in scaling SaaS applications today? Let’s discuss and learn from each other.

Presented by T-Mobile for Business
Small and mid-sized businesses are adopting AI at a pace that would have seemed unrealistic even a few years ago.
